word:greek-nt:G0037.explanation: Hagiazo means to make holy, set apart as holy, or treat as holy. It describes an altar sanctifying a gift and people being sanctified through truth.

word:greek-nt:G0042.explanation: Hagiosyne means holiness, a holy or sanctified state.

word:greek-nt:G0239.explanation: “Hallelujah” is a praise exclamation—a word spoken or sung to express worship. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs four times, all in Revelation 19, where it is repeated as part of heavenly praise. The word functions as a direct expression of joyful adoration rather than as a person’s name, place, or ordinary description. Its repeated use gives it the character of a communal cry of praise. The Greek New Testament preserves this brief worshipful expression as “hallelujah.”

word:greek-nt:G0305.explanation: Anabainō means to go up, mount, or ascend.

word:greek-nt:G0433.explanation: This word means “be fitting”: to be suitable, appropriate, or properly belonging in a situation. It expresses what is proper or becoming rather than merely what is possible. In the Greek New Testament, it appears three times, each in a different verse, so its precise force depends on the sentence and surrounding context. The word is used in Ephesians, Colossians, and Philemon, where it identifies conduct or action considered appropriate to the circumstances. Its central idea remains the same: something accords with what is proper or fitting.

word:greek-nt:G0495.explanation: Antipera means on the opposite side or shore, across from something.

word:greek-nt:G0510.explanation: This word means “interior,” referring to what is inside or toward the inner part of something. It describes an inward location or direction rather than something external. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 19:1. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain precisely how the word functions there, but its basic sense remains focused on what is within or farther inside. [p03:word:greek-nt:G0510:identity] [p03:word:greek-nt:G0510:occurrences] [p01:word:greek-nt:G0510:reference:0]

word:greek-nt:G0701.explanation: Arestos means pleasing, satisfactory, or acceptable.

word:greek-nt:G0778.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to strive”: to make a deliberate, earnest effort toward a goal. It describes purposeful exertion rather than a casual attempt, so it can express a person’s resolve to pursue something faithfully. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Acts 24:16. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense is active, intentional effort.

word:greek-nt:G0796.explanation: Astrape means a flash of lightning or lightning.

word:greek-nt:G0819.explanation: Atimia means dishonor and can describe a dishonorable use.

word:greek-nt:G0936.explanation: Basileuō means to rule or reign, including to reign over others.

word:greek-nt:G1113.explanation: This word describes a person who complains or grumbles—“a murmurer” or “grumbler.” It refers to someone whose speech expresses dissatisfaction rather than grateful acceptance. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Jude 1:16, and is rendered “murmurers.” Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is a person known for grumbling complaints.

word:greek-nt:G1225.explanation: Diaballō means to accuse; here, an accusation is made against a manager.

word:greek-nt:G1283.explanation: Diarpazō means to plunder or rob thoroughly.

word:greek-nt:G1328.explanation: Diermēneutēs means an interpreter—the person whose absence requires a speaker to keep silent in the assembly.

word:greek-nt:G1449.explanation: Engraphō means to write or inscribe.

word:greek-nt:G1517.explanation: Eirēnopoieō means to make peace or reconcile.

word:greek-nt:G1562.explanation: Ekdyo means to take off or strip off clothing.

word:greek-nt:G1643.explanation: Elaunein means to drive or propel. It can also mean to row.

word:greek-nt:G1706.explanation: Empiptō means to fall into something, whether a literal pit or a harmful condition.

word:greek-nt:G1845.explanation: This word refers to an exorcist—someone who attempts to drive out evil spirits. It describes a person identified by this activity, rather than naming the spirit or the person being delivered. In the Greek New Testament, the word occurs once, in Acts 19:13. Its basic meaning is therefore a person who practices or claims to practice the removal of evil spirits. The surrounding verse provides the specific setting for its use.

word:greek-nt:G1908.explanation: This word means “to mistreat”: to treat someone badly or unfairly. It describes harmful treatment directed toward another person, rather than ordinary disagreement or simple neglect. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, so its meaning is clear but its use is limited to two occurrences. The surrounding verse determines the particular circumstances, while the central idea remains wrongful treatment of someone.

word:greek-nt:G1971.explanation: Epipotheō means to long for or desire greatly.

word:greek-nt:G2004.explanation: Epitassō means to give an order or command. It can describe directing people to sit down or ordering an unclean spirit to leave.

word:greek-nt:G2156.explanation: Euschēmonōs means decently or properly, in a fitting way.

word:greek-nt:G2273.explanation: Etoi means whether, introducing an alternative between two possibilities.

word:greek-nt:G2350.explanation: Thorybeō means to disturb greatly or cause an uproar. It can also describe being troubled or agitated.

word:greek-nt:G2387.explanation: Jambres is a personal name identifying an individual mentioned in the Greek New Testament. It is not presented as a general word describing an action, quality, or object, but as the name by which this person is identified. The name occurs once, in 2 Timothy 3:8. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself functions simply as a person’s name.

word:greek-nt:G2509.explanation: Kathaper means “even as” or “just as.” It connects one statement with a comparison, as one body is described through its many members.

word:greek-nt:G2615.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to enslave” or “to make a slave.” It describes placing a person in the condition of slavery or bringing that person under a slave’s status. The word occurs twice in the Greek New Testament, once in 2 Corinthians 11:20 and once in Galatians 2:4. Its precise force in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and passage, but its central idea is clear: making someone a slave.

word:greek-nt:G2732.explanation: Katoikētērion means a habitation, dwelling place, or abode.

word:greek-nt:G2747.explanation: Kenchreai is Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.

word:greek-nt:G2790.explanation: Kitharoidos means a harpist, one who sings with a harp as accompaniment.

word:greek-nt:G2853.explanation: Kollao means to join oneself closely, cleave, or adhere to someone or something. It can also describe keeping company with others, as in joining oneself to another person.

word:greek-nt:G2974.explanation: Kōphos means deaf. It can also describe someone mute or unable to speak.

word:greek-nt:G3029.explanation: Lian means very, greatly, or exceedingly, marking a high degree. It marks anger as exceedingly great, amazement as very strong, and whiteness as especially intense.

word:greek-nt:G3160.explanation: Mattatha is a personal name, so it identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Greek New Testament, this name occurs once, in Luke 3:31, and it is rendered as “Mattatha.” Because the word functions as a name, its meaning is chiefly the person it designates, while the surrounding verse supplies the details about that person.

word:greek-nt:G3331.explanation: Metathesis means change or transformation. It can also mean removal.

word:greek-nt:G3348.explanation: Metechein means to share in, participate, or partake of something.

word:greek-nt:G3454.explanation: Mythos means an idle tale, fable, or fanciful story.

word:greek-nt:G3616.explanation: This word means “to manage a house” or “to manage one’s home.” It describes the work of overseeing and caring for a household. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Timothy 5:14. Its basic focus is domestic management: directing the affairs of the home rather than referring simply to living in a house. The surrounding verse supplies the specific force of the word there.

word:greek-nt:G3779.explanation: Houtōs means thus, so, or in this manner. It points to an action or situation corresponding to what has just been described, as when the Son gives life in the same way the Father raises the dead.

word:greek-nt:G3807.explanation: This word means “guardian” or “guardians”—someone entrusted to watch over and direct another person. It describes a responsible caretaker rather than merely a companion or observer. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs three times, all in 1 Corinthians and Galatians. Its precise role in each passage depends on the surrounding context, but its central idea remains responsible oversight and care. The word is used for a person who exercises guardianship for a time or purpose.

word:greek-nt:G3955.explanation: Parrēsiazomai means to speak freely or boldly.

word:greek-nt:G4077.explanation: Pege means a fountain, spring, or well. It can also refer to a flow.

word:greek-nt:G4154.explanation: Pneō means to blow, as wind does.

word:greek-nt:G4316.explanation: This word means “to designate”: it refers to identifying someone or something by a name or title. Its basic function is to mark out a person or thing through a stated designation, so readers can understand that a particular name or title has been assigned to the one being discussed. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Hebrews 5:10. The surrounding verse context is needed to explain its particular force there.

word:greek-nt:G4381.explanation: This word describes one who shows favoritism—a prejudiced person who treats people unfairly because of who they are. It refers to judging or receiving people with partiality rather than treating them impartially. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 10:34, so its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage. Its central idea is clear: a person who favors some people over others instead of dealing fairly with all.

word:greek-nt:G4460.explanation: Rhaab is the personal name Rahab, a woman who received the spies.

word:greek-nt:G4529.explanation: Salamis is a proper name identifying a place called “Salamis.” In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Acts 13:5, and the English rendering preserves the name rather than translating it into a descriptive word. Because no surrounding verse text is available here, the particular setting or significance of Salamis in Acts should not be inferred from the name alone. It functions as a place-name in that passage.

word:greek-nt:G4648.explanation: Skopeō means to look at carefully, take heed, or watch out.

word:greek-nt:G4785.explanation: Synkatapsephizomai means to be counted or numbered with others.

word:greek-nt:G4846.explanation: Sympnigō means to choke utterly, as weeds choke plants. It can also describe a crowd pressing in on someone.

word:greek-nt:G4903.explanation: Synergeō means to cooperate or work together.

word:greek-nt:G5030.explanation: Tacheōs means soon, quickly, or hastily.

word:greek-nt:G5092.explanation: Timē means a price. It also means honor.

word:greek-nt:G5236.explanation: Hyperbolē means excess or surpassing excellence—something beyond measure or of exceptional quality.

word:greek-nt:G5319.explanation: Phaneroō means to make something clear, visible, or known—to reveal or manifest it. It can describe hidden things being brought to light. It can also describe a person revealing himself openly.

word:greek-nt:G5463.explanation: Chairo means to rejoice or be glad. It can also be used as a salutation, meaning “Hail.”

word:greek-nt:G5566.explanation: Chōros means the northwest wind or the quarter of the sky from which it comes.

word:greek-nt:G5588.explanation: Psithuristēs means a whisperer or secret slanderer.

word:greek-nt:G5618.explanation: Hōsper means just as or even as. It marks a comparison, showing one situation as corresponding to another.

word:greek-nt:G6035.explanation: This word means “accursed”: regarded as under a curse or subject to divine condemnation. It is an adjective, describing a person or thing as standing in that condition rather than naming an action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at John 7:49. Its exact force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central meaning remains a solemn description of someone viewed as cursed or rejected under judgment.
